page: Microsoft Azure FX2mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a high base clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a massive 260 MB L3 cache, alongside 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches. The instance is equipped with 42.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core. It also includes 118 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Due to its high 4.2 GHz clock speed, the server achieves top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2355.0 and strong single-threaded compression and decompression results, such as 34.59 GB/sec for gzip and 14.46 GB/sec for bzip3. However, because it relies on a single physical core, multi-core and parallelized performance is limited. Multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the weak to poor categories. Memory bandwidth is also relatively constrained, with uncached large-block read speeds at 21.69 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.62 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX2mds_v2 offers a specialized resource profile, providing a high density of memory and high single-core clock speeds relative to its low vCPU count. This makes it a qualitatively cost-effective choice for workloads that require substantial memory capacity but do not scale across many parallel threads. It is well-suited for single-threaded database operations, memory-bound applications with low concurrency, lightweight text processing, and small-scale LLM inference tasks where single-core execution speed is critical.
